references.text: God's promise to Abraham that all the families of the earth shall be blessed through him, pointing forward to the proclamation of the gospel for all nations ([ref:Gen 12:3|Genesis 12:3]).
Isaiah's prophecy that the law shall go out from Zion and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem, corresponding to the proclamation beginning in Jerusalem ([ref:Isa 2:3|Isaiah 2:3]).

The Lord's servant shall be a light for the nations, so that salvation may reach to the ends of the earth — parallel to the preaching of repentance and forgiveness of sins to all nations ([ref:Isa 49:6|Isaiah 49:6]).

Jeremiah's prophecy of the new covenant in which the Lord will forgive their wrongdoing and remember their sin no more, pointing toward the proclamation of forgiveness of sins in Jesus' name ([ref:Jer 31:34|Jeremiah 31:34]).
Daniel's prophecy to put an end to transgression and make atonement for iniquity, pointing toward the forgiveness of sins proclaimed in the Messiah's name ([ref:Dan 9:24|Daniel 9:24]).
Micah's prophecy that the law shall go out from Zion and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem, parallel to the proclamation beginning in Jerusalem ([ref:Mic 4:2|Micah 4:2]).
Jesus' mission command to make disciples of all nations, which parallels the preaching of repentance and forgiveness of sins to all nations ([ref:Matt 28:19-20|Matthew 28:19-20]).
Jesus' commission to go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature, parallel to the proclamation for all nations ([ref:Mark 16:15|Mark 16:15]).
Jesus says that his disciples shall be his witnesses in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and to the ends of the earth — this unfolds the words about beginning from Jerusalem ([ref:Acts 1:8|Acts 1:8]).
Peter's proclamation on Pentecost where he calls for repentance and baptism in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins — a direct fulfillment of Luke 24:47 ([ref:Acts 2:38|Acts 2:38]).
Peter preaches to Cornelius that all the prophets testify that everyone who believes in Jesus receives forgiveness of sins through his name ([ref:Acts 10:43|Acts 10:43]).
Paul proclaims in Antioch of Pisidia that it is through Jesus that forgiveness of sins is proclaimed, in line with the commission in Luke 24:47 ([ref:Acts 13:38|Acts 13:38]).

Paul testifies that he preached repentance first in Damascus, then in Jerusalem and to the Gentiles — a fulfillment that the proclamation should begin from Jerusalem and reach all peoples ([ref:Acts 26:20|Acts 26:20]).
